proof_summary: Choose the least \(K\) with \(K^3\ge n^2\) and take all integers up to \(K\) together with all primes up to \(n\); for each \(m\le n\), its largest divisor \(d\le K\) has complementary factor either at most \(K\) or prime, since compositeness would force \((K+1)^3\le n^2\le K^3\). A central-binomial/Chebyshev estimate gives \(n^2\le 8(\pi(n)+1)^3\), hence \(K\le2(\pi(n)+1)\) and the covering set has size at most \(5\pi(n)\).
